source_cards.title: C1 Plates moving apart
source_cards.text: Use D1. Earth’s stiff outer layer is split into plates. They move slowly. At a divergent boundary, plates pull apart. Rock can crack or slip, causing shallow earthquakes. Hot mantle rock rises. As pressure falls, some rock melts. The magma can rise and erupt. Many such boundaries lie under the sea.

source_cards.title: C2 One plate sinking
source_cards.text: Use D2. At some convergent boundaries, an ocean plate sinks beneath another plate. This is subduction. Parts of the fault can lock while the plates keep moving. Strain builds in the rock. When the fault slips, energy travels as waves. This causes an earthquake. Water from the sinking plate helps hot mantle rock melt. Magma can rise and form volcanoes above the sinking plate.

source_cards.title: C3 Plates sliding past
source_cards.text: Use D3. At a transform boundary, plates slide past one another. Friction can hold parts of the fault still. Strain builds. A sudden slip sends out earthquake waves. Volcanoes are not usual at this type of boundary. The movement does not pull a gap open or push a plate deep into the mantle.

source_cards.title: C4 Japan earthquake example
source_cards.text: Tohoku region, Japan. 11 March 2011. The Pacific plate sinks beneath northern Japan. Parts of this boundary had locked. The plates kept moving, so strain built up. A large part of the fault then slipped. Energy spread as waves and caused strong shaking. This explains why the earthquake occurred near a subduction boundary. The earthquake had a magnitude of 9.1 in the current event record. It was not caused by hot weather or an eruption.

source_cards.title: C5 Pattern and limits
source_cards.text: Many earthquakes and volcanoes occur near plate boundaries. The pattern has a cause: plates meet and move there. Earthquakes can also occur inside plates. Some volcanoes form above hot spots away from boundaries. Where two continents collide, earthquakes can occur without a chain of volcanoes. A boundary map shows a broad pattern. It cannot tell the exact time of the next earthquake.
